source.title: Kindling in neural systems: progressive adversarial sensitization during LLM alignment mirrors psychiatric progression

record.file_problem: The main manuscript is present and readable, but cited Appendices A and B are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether iterative preference-style tuning changes harmful-request compliance using a different recipe from the original fine-tuning claim: ten rounds of supervised fine-tuning on chosen synthetic preference responses, with biased and balanced data conditions. It does not test the first-token KL or bypass claims.
record.gate_note: The study measures jailbreak rates for strong, medium and weak adversarial prompts during iterative tuning. Biased training includes a 30% harmlessness component that sometimes favours less safe responses; it is not a direct study of fine-tuning on a specified few-to-hundreds of harmful examples. Balanced No-Mitigation is a safety-preserving synthetic preference control, not ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning. No first-token KL, compliant-prefill, suffix, decoding-change, or localization-in-weights result is reported. The optional judge audit is described qualitatively, but its appendix is absent.
record.test_reason: The study tracks jailbreak compliance in safety-tuned chat models (TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct) over 10 cycles of chosen-response SFT. The biased data include ~60 pairs per cycle whose chosen answer softens refusal. That is a different recipe aimed at V1's question. The balanced arm mixes benign, honesty and refusal-reinforcing pairs, so it bears only weakly on V2. Nothing on per-token KL, prefilling or suffixes, weight localization, causes of shallowness, or deepening.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. Also add: the balanced control rose only mildly (10.1% to 17.1%), so the authors conclude that data content, not repeated updates alone, drove most of the erosion. The Qwen2.5-3B replication reproduced the condition ordering.
record.recipe_differences: Ten iterative rounds of chosen-response supervised fine-tuning on synthetic preference pairs, rather than the original fine-tuning recipe. The study uses intentionally biased and balanced data, LoRA adaptation, and mitigation arms; it is not full RLHF, PPO, or DPO.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varied by training condition, mitigation type, prompt strength, and model. Replay-only worsened weak-prompt outcomes, continuous regrowth attenuated them but allowed late overall rebound, and combined regrowth plus replay kept weak-prompt outcomes near or below balanced control. The Qwen model was quantized to 4-bit.

fits_no_version.finding: Sparse LoRA regrowth plus replay kept final jailbreak rates near or below the balanced control under biased tuning. Replay of refusal data alone did not protect and ended highest.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mitigation of iterative harmful-tuning drift: sparse regrowth plus replay suppresses it, replay alone does not.

record.problems: Five seeds; only compact 1.1B and 3B models; synthetic preference data and chosen-response SFT rather than full RLHF; no real-preference-data results; hand-crafted rule-based jailbreak scoring with low-to-moderate judge agreement on edge cases; aggregate-rate mixed-effects analysis rather than per-prompt models; mitigation components are not causally isolated because regrowth conditions use sparse LoRA masks from the start. The authors also note that capability probes are small and that results should be treated as preliminary.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the reported per-cycle overall trajectories, strong-prompt outcomes, sycophancy outcomes, threshold diagnostics other than weak-prompt AUC, and qualitative supplementary LLM-judge audit; the included final overall/weak rates and weak-prompt AUC were prioritized for V1/V2. The supplementary audit is single-seed and its cited appendix is absent from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Fine-tuning on a small, specified set of explicitly harmful examples; near-total removal of refusal; models above 3B; full RLHF, DPO or PPO.
Ordinary benign instruction data without safety pairs; carefully chosen benign data; real preference data.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefill, suffix or decoding attacks.
LoRA sparsity is used as a mitigation substrate; there is no test of where safety resides in the weights.
Regrowth and replay are mitigations for drift, not training that spreads safety beyond the first tokens.

missing.what: Mixed-effects model of weak-prompt jailbreak rate. Reference-arm (balanced) cycle term 0.003, p=.041; Biased No-Mitigation cycle interaction 0.015, p<.001.

Cycle-0 weak-prompt and strong-prompt jailbreak rates are not reported for either model. Final strong JB for Biased No-Mitigation is 48.0% vs 32.0% balanced on TinyLlama; strong outcomes are declared left out.
LLM-judge agreement with the rule-based scorer was low to moderate. The absolute rates depend on the keyword-based scorer.

record.verdict_notes: The biased data are ~70% sycophantic benign pairs and ~30% pairs whose chosen answer partially complies with questionable requests; this is closest to V1, but not the original harmful-example attack. The balanced arm contains explicit refusal training, so it is a weak test of V2. Mitigation arms are relinked to none as the study's own defence. Scoring is rule-based with temperature-0.7 sampling, and Qwen was run 4-bit quantized.

versions.untested_parts: Tests synthetic biased preference-style tuning that sometimes favours less safe responses, not direct fine-tuning on a specified few-to-hundreds of harmful examples. Does not show refusal being removed almost entirely.
Tests repeated balanced, safety-preserving synthetic preference-style SFT, not ordinary benign instruction fine-tuning or a range of carefully chosen benign datasets.
No compliant opening prefill, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change intervention.
LoRA is used, but the study does not test whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Does not test whether a data or objective property causes first-token shallowness.
Regrowth and replay are tested as mitigation for iterative drift, not as training to spread safety beyond early response tokens or as a test of whether such deepening holds up.

relationships.reason: Tuning on refusal-softening chosen responses raised jailbreak rates. TinyLlama overall went from 12.5% to 38.4% (Qwen 35.5% vs 18.3% balanced). Weak-prompt AUC was about twice the balanced control in both models (TL_biased_overall, TL_biased_weak, TL_AUC_biased, Q_biased_overall, Q_biased_weak, Q_AUC_biased).
relationships.display_finding: TinyLlama's overall jailbreak rate went from 12.5% to 38.4%, Qwen's was 35.5% against 18.3% under balanced tuning, and weak-prompt AUC was about twice the balanced control in both models.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: TL_biased_overall and Q_biased_overall show partial erosion after ten cycles containing 2,000 total pairs and approximately 600 refusal-softening pairs. TL_biased_weak, Q_biased_weak, TL_AUC_biased and Q_AUC_biased corroborate increased vulnerability, but do not establish V1's few-to-few-hundred-example claim.

relationships.reason: Compliance stayed near baseline through cycle 5 (12.5% to 16.3%, Table 5) despite ~300 harmful-leaning pairs. It reached only 38.4% overall and 22.4% on weak prompts by cycle 10, far from near-total (TL_biased_overall, TL_biased_weak).
relationships.display_finding: Compliance stayed near baseline through cycle 5 (12.5% to 16.3%) despite about 300 harmful-leaning pairs, and by cycle 10 reached only 38.4% overall and 22.4% on weak prompts.
